parole.significato: fracture (having a fracture of such a form)
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κλᾰ́σῐς (klắsĭs, “breaking, fracture”) (via French -clase), from κλάω (kláō, “I break”).
Representing the Ancient Greek πτῐ́λον (ptĭ́lon, “feather”, “down”; “leaf”); in the botanical sense denoting leaves, probably after the French -ptile. Compare ptilo-.
First attested in 1820. From biblio- + -phile (from Ancient Greek βιβλίον (biblíon, “paper, document, tablet”) + φίλος (phílos, “beloved”)), probably after French bibliophile.

parole.significato: Any of a group of saints depicted in art carrying heads in their hands.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek κεφαλή (kephalḗ, “head”) + -φόρος (-phóros, “bearing”), a derivative of φέρω (phérō, “I bear, I carry”); in the Christian sense, via French céphalophore, coined by Marcel Hébert in 1914.

parole.significato: A pointed sheath that protects the emerging shoot in monocotyledons such as oats and grasses.
parole.testo: A classical compound of the Ancient Greek κολεός (koleós, “sheath”) + the English -ptile (“leaf”) – the suffix representing the Ancient Greek πτῐ́λον (ptĭ́lon) – probably after the French coléoptile.

parole.significato: Of or pertaining to a despot or tyrant.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek δεσποτικός (despotikós) via French despotique, equivalent to despot + -ic.

parole.significato: Native to a particular area or culture; originating where it occurs.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἐν (en, “in”) + δῆμος (dêmos, “people”) + -ic. Possibly via Ancient Greek ἔνδημος (éndēmos, “among one's people, at home, native”) and/or French endémique. By surface analysis, en- + demic.

parole.significato: An astronomical instrument, based on a telescope, for measuring the diameter of the sun; now used to measure the angula…
parole.testo: From helio- + -meter, from Ancient Greek Ἥλιος (Hḗlios), from ἥλιος (hḗlios, “sun”), and French mètre, from Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron, “measure”).

parole.significato: A line on a surface (such as the Earth) that cuts all meridians at a constant angle (but not a right angle) – on Earth,…
parole.testo: Back-formation from loxodromic, from Ancient Greek λοξός (loxós, “oblique”) + δρόμος (drómos, “course”) via French.

parole.significato: One with an abnormal fondness of music; a person who loves music.
parole.testo: From melo- (prefix meaning “music”) (from Ancient Greek μέλος (mélos, “song; melody, tune”)) + -maniac (from French maniaque, from Late Latin maniacus, from Ancient Greek μανιακός (maniakós), an adjectival form of μανία (manía, “madness; mad desire, compulsion”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European
From Ancient Greek ὄμφαξ (ómphax, “unripe fruit, especially grapes”): compare French omphacin.
From tropho- + Ancient Greek σπέρμα (spérma, “seed”). Compare French trophosperme.
